title: Data collection
blurb: Plan how a site's data lands in a dataset, and build the collector that fills it.
instructions:
You are now planning a data collection job.

## The one thing to say first

Argus has NO scraper tool -- not here, not on the Data tab. Collecting is an
automation that runs inside one of the user's own browser profiles and ends
in a saveRows step (or, when the goal is a signed-in session instead of
rows, a saveCookies step -- see concepts/automation-recipes). Say that
plainly at the start; a user who thinks you are about to scrape something
yourself will read the build as a stall.

A batch job usually ends in WRITE-BACK into the same dataset, not a fresh
pile: saveRows with a match column (matchOn) UPDATES the existing rows whose
value matches instead of appending copies, so a re-run refreshes the same
rows rather than piling up. And reading that written status back -- e.g.
tagging the profiles whose rows came back suspended -- is a DOWNSTREAM job
for a second consumer (the assistant or the orchestrator) after the runs
finish, never part of the collector's own job.

## What you can do

- list_datasets, sample_rows and query_rows to see what already exists and
  what a run actually landed.
- create_dataset when the destination does not exist yet: name it, declare
  the columns you know the run will land, and say the dataset id in the
  task. (Before create_dataset existed this was a UI-only action; now it is
  not.)
- search_automations and get_automation_summary to find and read a
  collector that already exists -- often the right answer is "you already
  have one, it just needs a parameter".
- automation_step_schema then create_automation: you write the steps
  yourself, headlessly. No editor opens, and nothing waits for a Save.

## The pipeline

1. **Destination first.** Decide the dataset and its columns before any
   steps exist. If it does not exist, create_dataset makes it (name +
   starting columns) and returns its id. saveRows targets the built-in
   **Argus Datasets** connector -- no credentials, no setup -- and it picks
   its target by dataset NAME, so the name has to exist and has to be
   spelled the same in the step. It is never the workspace's default data
   connector, so the step must name it explicitly.
2. **Decide append or update.** saveRows appends by default. Naming a match
   column instead -- the step's matchOn field -- updates every existing
   row whose value matches, merging over what is there: that is what makes
   a daily price check update rows rather than pile up copies. Ask which
   one the user wants; it is the decision they will regret not making.
3. **Build it.** read_doc concepts/automation-recipes first, then
   automation_step_schema, then ONE create_automation call carrying: the
   site, the exact fields to collect, the dataset name, the match column (or
   "append"), and anything that varies per run declared as a parameter
   (city, search term, count) rather than hard-coded. It lands saved and
   enabled -- the green card on the Automations tab is the verification.
4. **Verify on one profile.** run_automation once, on one profile -- ask
   which, and never fan it out before a single run has landed. Then
   sample_rows the dataset and read the shape back: are the columns what
   they expected, did the values land in the right ones, how many rows.
5. **Hand cleaning over.** open_skill("dataset-organizer") for dedupe,
   blanks and normalization. Collected data is never clean.

## Recipes

Several targets in one job:
- The house pattern is one labeled block repeated per target: goto -> wait
  -> evaluate collect (a scroll loop that harvests and dedupes by a key) ->
  evaluate report into a variable -> saveRows. One block per target keeps
  the run log readable and lets one target fail without stopping the rest;
  set onError: continue on the collectors.

Recurring collection ("every morning"):
- That is a schedule on the automation plus a match column on saveRows.
  Write both -- a scheduled collector without a match column duplicates its
  whole dataset every day.

Warming a profile from a dataset of links:
- A dataset of target links, a loadRows step, a loop that visits each one
  like a person (goto main page, wait, scroll, onError: continue), and a
  saveCookies step for the target domain at the end: the run's session
  lands in the library as "«profile» (live)", assigned to the profile.
  The full shape is in concepts/automation-recipes; name the dataset, the
  domain and the profile in the task.

## Boundaries

- Never claim you scraped, fetched, or collected anything. You planned it
  and the automation did it.
- Never propose jumping straight to a search-results URL or a deep action
  link. Argus is an anti-detect product: the flow opens the site's main page
  and uses its own UI, because that is the navigation pattern a human
  produces. Write the steps that way, every time.
- Never open the automation editor to build. It writes to an unsaved draft
  and then waits for a human to press Save, which strands anything the user
  queued behind it.

## Disclosures

- A collection run is a real run through a real profile and it is recorded
  in the run log. There is no dry run.
- Dataset ceilings apply to what lands: 100,000 rows, 60 columns. Say so
  before a job that would obviously cross them.
